Sedno privacy policy

Version: 23 October 2026

Controller and contact

Controller: Mariusz Bąbka, an individual, ul. Słowiańska 91, Modlniczka, Poland. For privacy and account deletion, contact contact@sedno.xyz. The controller has not appointed a data protection officer.

This policy covers the Sedno app and support for its users. Poland is the first selected market. The app is for people aged 13 and over. People aged 13–17 should use it with permission from a parent or guardian. The app does not check your age or collect your date of birth.

The full Polish privacy policy is available at https://sedno.xyz/prywatnosc/ and in the app. This English version is available in the app. A short Polish summary is at https://sedno.xyz/#prywatnosc. Account deletion instructions in Polish are at https://sedno.xyz/usun-konto. The server has been running since 19 October 2026.

Text and artificial intelligence

Your text will be sent through the Sedno server to the AI provider, OpenAI, to simplify or correct it. Do not enter information you do not want to share. Photos stay on your device. Speech is recognised on your device; only text is sent to AI. Reading aloud uses a downloaded English voice on your phone. AI can make mistakes. Check the result.

When you choose Simplify or Correct, your text is sent through the Sedno server to the OpenAI Responses API. The result returns to the app. The Sedno server uses the content to handle your request, but does not save the original or result in its database or logs. We do not send your whole history or photos.

Disabling response storage in the API does not mean the provider retains no data. OpenAI does not use API data to train models by default. Safety logs may contain content for up to 30 days, with exceptions set by the provider. Caching may retain temporary state. We do not claim zero retention or that OpenAI processes data only within the European Union.

Do not send information about health, disability or other specially protected information. Before sending, remove unnecessary personal data and other people's data. Using Sedno does not mean consenting to the processing of all categories of data.

Deleting your account and data

We will delete your Sedno account, its data on the server and local history on this device. This cannot be undone. Deleting your account does not cancel your subscription. To stop charges, open Google Play → Payments and subscriptions → Subscriptions → Sedno → Cancel subscription.

In the app, choose Account → Delete account → Delete account and data. After successful deletion, we remove your Sedno identity in Firebase, account sessions, linked installations, request metadata and purchase records from the Sedno database. We do not delete your Google account.

Without the app, email contact@sedno.xyz with the subject “Sedno account deletion”. Provide the email address you use to sign in. Do not send passwords, sign-in codes, tokens, identity documents, photos or texts to simplify or correct. Sending the email alone does not delete your account. We will confirm that you control the account before deleting it. If there is doubt, we will ask only for extra information needed for verification.

Deleting your account by email or on another device does not remove history on your other devices. Delete it in History or clear app data in Android settings. We have no remote access to local history. Purchases and data retained by Google are subject to Google's policies.

Photos, voice and history on your device

Photos, cropping and text recognition are processed on your device. Sedno does not send photos to its server or the AI provider. Recognised text is submitted directly for simplification. After an error or cancellation, you can edit it. After recognition, cancellation or an error, the app attempts to delete working copies of the photo. Abruptly stopping the app may interrupt cleanup. Separate copies saved by a camera app remain under your control.

The microphone recognises speech locally in the selected language on supported devices with Android 13 or later and a downloaded language model. Audio is processed in device memory, without saving a recording or sending it to the Sedno server or OpenAI. Recording ends after 1.5 seconds of silence following speech or after at most 60 seconds. Recognised text is sent for simplification through the server and OpenAI, like text from a photo. Stop cancels the session. You can refuse microphone access and still type text or use the camera.

Reading text aloud in Correct mode happens on your device. Sedno selects a downloaded voice for the selected language that does not need an internet connection. Text is not sent to the Sedno server or OpenAI for reading aloud. If no suitable voice is available, reading will not start. Downloading a speech recognition model or voice in Android settings may need internet access and is subject to the speech engine provider's policies.

History contains the original text, the simplified or corrected result, the selected mode, the processing language and the date. It is encrypted, local and excluded from Android backups. Entries expire after 7 days. Expired entries are not shown; cleanup runs when history is read, when the app starts and when it resumes. If the app is closed, deletion happens at the next such event. You can delete entries earlier. Signing out clears local history.

The device also stores a protected session, a random installation identifier and, if you choose one, your language preference. Deleting your account does not remove the random installation identifier from your device. You can remove it by clearing app data in Android.

Account, limits and subscription

You can start without an account. Firebase Authentication handles optional sign-in through Google or email and password. Sedno saves your Firebase UID, sign-in method and account creation date. The Sedno server does not receive your Google or Firebase password. Google may process your email, profile data, IP address and connection data needed for sign-in.

To protect the service and track limits, we store pseudonymous installation, session and request data, their dates, statuses and an HMAC fingerprint of the text. The fingerprint is not a copy of the text. The installation identifier is pseudonymous, not anonymous. Signing in does not give you a new free allowance. Your IP address is used to limit request rates. It is not a field in the Sedno database, but infrastructure providers may process it. Google Play Integrity checks app and device authenticity without receiving text or photos.

Google Play handles payments and subscriptions. Sedno does not receive your card number or bank account details. The Sedno database stores an encrypted purchase token, its hash, its account link, entitlement status and expiry, and verification data. Separate purchase notification identifiers prevent events from being processed twice.

Providers and technical data

OpenAI handles text simplification and correction through its API. For a standard customer agreement in Poland, OpenAI's terms name OpenAI Ireland Ltd as the contracting entity. The provider processes content to deliver the service and data needed for safety under its terms.

Google provides Firebase Authentication, Google Sign-In, ML Kit, Play Integrity and Google Play. Google Ireland Limited and Google LLC participate in providing services under the terms of the relevant products. OVHcloud provides the controller's email service in the sedno.xyz domain.

ML Kit recognises text on your device. The SDK may send Google technical and usage metrics, such as installation identifiers, device model, app version, errors and execution time. On-device OCR does not mean that no such communication occurs. Photos and recognised content are not part of this telemetry. We do not integrate adverts, Firebase Analytics or Crashlytics.

Sedno infrastructure: Google Cloud Run for the server, Cloud Firestore Standard in the europe-central2 region (Warsaw), and Firebase Hosting for the API and documents. Under standard Google Cloud terms for a Polish billing address, the contracting entity is Google Cloud Poland Sp. z o.o. The server has been running since 19 October 2026. Running these resources does not confirm that all required agreements are in place or that pre-release checks are complete.

Purposes and legal bases

Simplifying or correcting text at your request, providing an account and managing subscription entitlement: Article 6(1)(b) GDPR — performing a service contract or taking steps at your request.

Security, abuse prevention and tracking limits: Article 6(1)(f) GDPR — the legitimate interest in protecting the service. We limit data to necessary metadata and do not use it for advertising. You may object; we will assess your specific situation.

Answering general questions and necessary troubleshooting: Article 6(1)(f) GDPR — communication and keeping the service working. Handling data rights: Article 6(1)(c) together with Articles 12–22 GDPR. A minimal record of handling a request demonstrates its completion under Articles 5(2) and 24 GDPR.

We do not treat installation, the AI notice or camera permission as consent to unrestricted processing. Any assessment of whether SDK diagnostics need separate consent to access the device must take place before enabling that feature in production. This policy does not replace any required consent mechanism.

Text and necessary technical data are needed to simplify or correct it. Account and purchase data are needed only when you use those features. The camera and microphone are optional: you can type or paste text. Sedno does not use advertising profiling or make decisions with legal effects based on simplified or corrected content. You can report an incorrect quota or service protection block to the controller.

Data outside the European Economic Area

Google and OpenAI services may process data outside the EEA, including in the USA. Firebase Authentication uses infrastructure in the USA. Locating the Sedno database in Warsaw does not mean all data stays in Poland or the EEA.

Production use requires data processing terms and appropriate transfer safeguards. Providers describe standard contractual clauses and adequacy decisions for recipients they cover. We do not claim that using the Google or OpenAI brand alone ensures a particular mechanism for every transfer. You can ask the controller for information about terms and a copy of the safeguards used. Public provider terms are listed at the end of this document.

Retention in the app and Sedno database

Text and results on the Sedno server: content is not saved; it is used in memory to handle your request. Local history: 7 days, with cleanup as described above. Request metadata and HMAC text fingerprints older than 8 days are removed by a separate hourly job, regardless of app traffic. Daily usage counters and quota reservations are retained for up to 8 days.

Account sessions are valid for 7 days and guest sessions for 90 days. The same hourly job deletes expired sessions. An expired session does not allow access, even before its record is physically deleted. An unlinked guest identity older than 90 days is deleted once it has no sessions or requests left. This may happen later than day 90.

Accounts, linked installations and Sedno purchase records are retained until account deletion. The current app does not automatically delete inactive accounts or expired purchase records. Technical Google Play notification identifiers currently have no automatic deletion deadline. They do not contain purchase tokens or account links. We do not claim retention periods that have not been implemented.

Selected operational retention rules

For production, we adopt these rules: technical logs and database backups up to 30 days; correspondence up to 90 days after a case closes; minimal confirmation of handling data rights up to 12 months after closure. Confirmation retains only the date, request type and outcome, without full correspondence. These are organisational rules. The main log store is set to 30 days. Backups of the previous SQL database do not cover Firestore. New backups and recovery need separate configuration; we do not claim they are automatically enabled. If enabled, the 30-day maximum applies. Other stores, exports and email handling rules need separate checks and implementation before public release.

Backups are for disaster recovery, not ongoing use of deleted accounts. After restoration, deletions must be applied again before data is made available. For a specific legal obligation or dispute, only necessary data may be retained for the period required by that obligation or case. We do not extend all retention unnecessarily.

Sedno's retention periods do not change provider periods. Firebase describes retaining sign-in IP addresses for several weeks and other authentication data until user deletion is requested; subsequent deletion from active systems and backups may take up to 180 days. OpenAI retention is described in the AI section. Google payment data and metrics follow the relevant service policies.

Your rights and contact

To the extent provided by the GDPR, you may request access to and a copy of your data, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and portability of relevant data. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests. If processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it without affecting earlier processing. Rights are subject to legal conditions and exceptions.

Email contact@sedno.xyz. We respond without undue delay, normally within one month of receiving your request. In cases allowed by the GDPR, this may be extended by two months; we will explain why within the first month. If there is reasonable doubt about your identity, we will ask for necessary confirmation without routinely requesting an identity document.

You can complain to the President of the Polish Personal Data Protection Office: https://uodo.gov.pl. A general message about your data does not require you to provide texts you simplify or correct.

Policy changes

Each version has a date. We will announce significant changes on the privacy page and in app update information before new processing starts. If a change needs consent, updating this document does not replace it. A change of provider, purpose or retention requires updated information and actual service configuration.
